items.title: Top 5 Most Tilted Planets (#1 Spins Upside Down) #shorts
items.description:
Earth is tilted 23.4°. Mars, Saturn and Neptune lean a little more. Uranus rolls on its side. And Venus is flipped completely upside down.

Full video on the channel: "How Long to Reach Every Planet? By Car, Neptune Takes 4,912 Years"

Sources:
- NASA planetary fact sheets (NSSDC), obliquity to orbit: Venus 177.4°, Uranus 97.8°, Neptune 28.3°, Saturn 26.7°, Mars 25.2°, Earth 23.4°, Jupiter 3.1°
- NASA Science: Venus spins backward (retrograde), so the Sun rises in the west
- NASA Science: Uranus rotates on its side; each pole gets about 42 years of continuous sunlight followed by 42 years of darkness
- NASA: Saturn's rings appeared edge-on from Earth in March 2025
- Own calculations: Neptune's 165-year orbit divided by 4 seasons = about 41 years; Mars minus Earth = 1.8°

Visuals are original. Narration uses a synthetic voice.
#shorts #space #planets #science

items.title: 764 Earths Fit Inside Saturn. It Would Still Float #shorts
items.description:
Saturn could swallow 764 Earths, yet a litre of it weighs less than a litre of water. In a big enough ocean, it would float.

Full video on the channel: "What If Earth Had Rings Like Saturn? It May Have Had One 466 Million Years Ago"

Sources:
- NASA Saturn Fact Sheet (NSSDC): mean radius 58,232 km, volume 763.59 times Earth's, mean density 687 kg per cubic metre
- NASA Earth Fact Sheet: mean radius 6,371 km, mean density 5,514 kg per cubic metre
- NASA Science: Saturn is the only planet in our solar system less dense than water
- Own calculations: (58,232 / 6,371)³ = 763.6 Earths; mean diameter = 9.1 Earths; a floating Saturn would sit 69% under the waterline (687 / 1,000)

Visuals are original. Narration uses a synthetic voice.
#shorts #space #saturn #science

items.title: All 8 Billion Humans Fit Inside a Sugar Cube #shorts
items.description:
Atoms are almost entirely empty space. Squeeze it out of all 8.2 billion of us and humanity shrinks to about 2 cubic centimetres, a sugar cube weighing half a billion tonnes. That's neutron star matter.

Full video on the channel: "What If We Swapped the Sun for 5 Other Stars? One Puts Earth INSIDE It"

Sources:
- United Nations, World Population Prospects 2024: world population about 8.2 billion
- Walpole et al. (2012), BMC Public Health, "The weight of nations": average adult body mass about 62 kg (used here for everyone, so the result is an upper bound)
- Nuclear saturation density: about 0.16 nucleons per cubic femtometre, about 2.7 × 10^17 kg per cubic metre
- Atoms are about 10^-10 m across, nuclei about 10^-15 m: the nucleus is about 1/100,000 of the atom's width
- NASA: a sugar cube of neutron-star material would weigh about a billion tons on Earth
- Own calculations: 8.2 billion × 62 kg = 5.1 × 10^11 kg; at nuclear density that is about 1.9 cubic centimetres; at the density of water it is 0.51 cubic kilometres, a cube about 800 m on a side

Visuals are original. Narration uses a synthetic voice.
#shorts #space #neutronstar #science
